sentiment.rationale: The company reported a modest beat on backward-looking metrics (comparable sales +0.6%, adjusted EPS +3.8% vs prior year), but full-year guidance was reaffirmed unchanged (sales $92B-$94B, comps flat to +2%, adjusted EPS $12.25-$12.75). Management explicitly flagged ongoing DIY pressure, a challenging housing environment, and near-term cost headwinds (transportation, tariffs) with no upward revision to forward expectations. The Q&A confirmed that the consumer environment is playing out as anticipated, not improving. This is a classic 'in-line quarter with stable guidance' — the default 0.0 score applies.

summary.revenue: Sales of $23.1 billion, up 10.3% from Q1 last year. Comparable sales increased 0.6%.
summary.eps: GAAP diluted EPS of $2.90; adjusted diluted EPS of $3.03, up 3.8% versus prior year ($2.92).
summary.guidance: Affirming fiscal 2026 outlook: sales $92B-$94B, comparable sales flat to +2%, adjusted operating margin 11.6%-11.8%, adjusted diluted EPS approximately $12.25-$12.75. Q2 comp sales expected roughly in line with full-year midpoint; Q2 adjusted EPS expected ~2% below prior year.
summary.margin: Gross margin 32.7%, down 70 bps (driven by FBM/ADG dilution, offset by credit revenue favorability). SG&A 19.2% of sales, leveraging 17 bps. Adjusted operating margin 11.5%, down 43 bps vs prior year.
key_risks: DIY demand remains under pressure, particularly in big-ticket discretionary categories.
Elevated interest rates, higher costs, and low housing turnover continue to challenge the housing market.
Near-term pressure from higher transportation costs (fuel, oil prices) impacting Q2.
Tariff environment (IEEPA, Section 122, 232, 301) creating inflation and supply chain uncertainty.
Challenging residential construction market affecting FBM and ADG acquisitions.
Pro customers concerned about growing labor costs and constrained labor market.
key_opportunities: Continued strength in Pro, Appliances, Online (+15.5% sales growth), and Home Services.
MyLowe's Pro Rewards loyalty program resonating with small-to-medium Pro customers.
Mylow AI shopping assistant driving triple the conversion rate for users vs non-users.
HomeCare+ subscription service for DIY customers, exclusive to MyLowe's Rewards members.
FBM and ADG acquisitions positioning Lowe's for future recovery in residential homebuilding.
Rollout of workwear and pet assortments to all stores by year-end.
Pro Extended Aisle initiative driving Pro plan sales and market share gains.
Potential tailwinds from tax refunds ($50B yet to be distributed) and HELOC activity ($35 trillion tappable equity).

management_tone.label: mixed
management_tone.justification: Management expresses confidence in execution and market share gains ('we're pleased with our performance,' 'we're well positioned') while simultaneously acknowledging persistent headwinds ('DIY demand remains under pressure,' 'the most difficult housing market since the financial crisis') and reaffirming rather than raising guidance.

evidence.quote: Sales for the first quarter were $23.1 billion, up 10.3% from Q1 last year, in line with expectations.
Comparable sales were up 0.6% driven by well-coordinated spring execution, including our SpringFest event, along with continued strength in Pro, Appliances, Online and Home Services.

evidence.quote: we delivered adjusted diluted earnings per share of $3.03, up 3.8% versus the prior year.

today, we are affirming our fiscal 2026 outlook. We continue to expect sales in the range of $92 billion to $94 billion, with comparable sales in a range of flat to up 2%. We expect adjusted operating margin in a range of 11.6% to 11.8% and full-year adjusted diluted earnings per share of approximately $12.25 to $12.75.
